extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders in Singapore online-safety policy (industry/platforms, civil society, victims, academics, government)
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of responses and government positions on proposed measures to enhance online safety in Singapore, including a new complaints agency, statutory torts for online harms, rules for disclosure of user information, and victim support. The page records stakeholder feedback and the Ministries' intended design principles and safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a dedicated complaints agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce a complaints mechanism administered by a new Agency to provide timely assistance to victims of online harms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: recognised need for a specialised body with relevant expertise to provide timely and effective assistance; would add credibility and reassurance; simplify seeking help without lengthy and expensive court processes; increase accessibility especially for the young and the elderly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency should adopt a balanced and proportionate approach
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency should adopt well-defined parameters and fair processes when addressing complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders sought clarifications on definitions and relationship to existing laws, transparent appeals mechanism, and realistic timelines for compliance; agency should work closely with industry partners and provide practical, workable directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of online harms set out in legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: Set out the definitions of online harms in legislation so that the elements of each online harm will be clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, provide illustrative examples and guidelines to explain the scope of online harms and how the agency would generally respond to archetypal complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible, efficient appeals process (independent panel + judicial review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide for complainants and persons directly affected by agency decisions to appeal to an independent panel; same persons may also apply for judicial review of the decision of the independent panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals must be fairly dealt with while being time and cost efficient; the aim is to avoid onerous processes that deter victims from seeking relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency directions must be practical and include reasonable timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed agency will issue directions that are practical and workable for recipients and provide reasonable timelines for compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This balances acting on online harms in a timely manner with avoiding onerous obligations; agency will work closely with industry partners in designing directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce statutory torts for specified online harms
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce statutory torts for various online harms to provide legal certainty and enable victims to pursue redress and compensation in court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: hold perpetrators accountable, deter harmful behaviour, provide compensation, and compel platforms to be accountable to their users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties calibrated by role (communicator, administrator, platform)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicators, administrators, and platforms should be subject to duties not to commit online harms or to act on harms brought to their notice, and may be sued for damages if they breach those duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duties are carefully calibrated to reflect respective roles in the online ecosystem; balance needed to avoid blurring communicator vs platform liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against defensive practices and over-removal of content
rubrics_metrics.description: Design obligations to avoid encouraging defensive practices and excessive removal of content by platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders warned that obligations could result in excessive content takedowns; the statutory torts should be calibrated to discourage that outcome while encouraging reasonable action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deterrence against frivolous and vexatious claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Include measures to discourage frivolous and vexatious complaints and litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vexatious complaints divert resources from genuine cases and must be addressed with suitably strong deterrent measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards to respect and preserve free expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Design safeguards so the statutory torts and agency processes do not stifle public discourse and free speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals contain safeguards to respect free expression; objective is to preserve ability to speak freely while reducing fear of online harms that inhibit participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify interaction with existing legal and regulatory framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide greater clarity on how the new measures interact and complement existing laws and how the agency will work with existing agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ministries will work towards explaining complementarities and coordination to ensure timely and effective handling using full complement of measures and powers available under the law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of perpetrator user information for specified purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose a perpetrator's user information to the victim for certain specified purposes (e.g. to bring a claim under statutory torts, safeguard oneself from the perpetrator) to improve accountability and deterrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Around 80% of respondents agreed disclosure could prevent anonymity being misused and meet victims' needs for protection and legal recourse; must be narrowly for specified purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict safeguards and penalties for misuse of disclosed information
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure disclosed user information is only used for permitted purposes and protect against misuse such as doxxing or vigilante justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguards include disclosure only to necessary parties, sensitive information handled only by authorised entities, and penalties for misuse; ensure balance between transparency and privacy protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure should comply with Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) and data minimisation
rubrics_metrics.description: All measures requiring collection and disclosure of user information must comply with existing data protection provisions including the Personal Data Protection Act 2012.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry noted difficulties due to platforms' data minimisation principles and foreign laws; agency will work with industry to ensure any requirements are workable and context-sensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit disclosure criteria and apply civil-procedure-like principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt stricter disclosure criteria and civil procedure principles to govern disclosure of user information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns included victim safety, protection, efficacy with anonymous accounts; suggestions included limiting handling to trusted entities and following civil disclosure principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguard legitimate anonymity (e.g., whistleblowing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect anonymity for legitimate purposes such as whistleblowing when designing disclosure and identification rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents emphasised that anonymity should be safeguarded for legitimate uses and that disclosure regimes should not erode legitimate protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design workable requirements for platforms to collect/disclose identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure requirements for platforms to collect and disclose user identity are workable in the Singapore context, taking into account platforms' constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency will work closely with industry partners to ensure any requirements are practical given platforms' data practices and foreign legal constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise accessibility and comprehensive victim support services
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure measures and support services are accessible to all victims and implement comprehensive victim support systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions include referrals to counselling and partnering with organisations that play important roles in the online safety ecosystem; develop a holistic approach that prioritises accessibility and victim support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid onerous, time-consuming processes to improve access to relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Design processes so victims are not dissuaded or deterred from seeking relief by onerous and time-consuming procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim of the dedicated agency is to enhance access to relief without forcing victims through lengthy and expensive court processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide special considerations for minors involved in online harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider special rules or considerations for minors who commit online harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders highlighted the need for special considerations for minors; policy design should account for age-related factors when imposing duties or remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration with industry and community partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency and measures should involve close cooperation with industry partners and community organisations to effectively address online harms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry are partners in the mission; agency will work with community partners to serve the public more effectively and take context into account before making directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of identification systems (e.g., SingPass) as a possible approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Some respondents suggested using SingPass for identification to aid disclosure and accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This suggestion is one option raised; policymakers must weigh consistency with offline approaches and privacy implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide illustrative examples and guidelines to explain scope and response
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate, provide illustrative examples and guidelines to explain the scope of online harms to be addressed and how the agency would generally respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps clarify vague or subjective harms and guide consistent application of statutory torts and agency responses.
